_doc: maturation_dispatch.py's settings (item RIMMANDRAKE_WIRE_DISPATCH_TO_LAUNCH_BUILDERS_MODS_SAT_IDLE). The owner, 2026-11-14 ~9 PM PST: "So can we wire up Operations/Dispatch such that they do advance on these offline builders? ... As long as we don't have automated loops rejecting/cycling things, we can't get into too much trouble."
_advancing_doc: The four by his card of 2026-11-14 (spec §5 Dispatch), Graffiti by his word the same night (it is at the Designer, which is never auto-launched), and Contagion by his order of 2026-11-15 ('pick the next most mature biome mod to add', item RIMMANDRAKE_ADMIT_CONTAGION_AS_NEXT_BIOME). Order is launch priority when slots are short, over every layer's launches (prioritise: a run that just ended keeps its mod's slot through settle_s). Pyrelands first by his card of 2026-11-17 ("Which mod gets the next run" at max_live 1 -> "Pyrelands (Recommended)").
_cap_model_doc: Every cap here (cap_usd, steward_cap_usd, fix_cap_usd, blind_cap_usd, ingame_cap_usd) was set from Opus 5.5 runs (mod_model.CAPS_PRICED_FOR). A mod whose builders are pinned to another model in the control store (`pipe model <Mod> fable|default`; item RIMMANDRAKE_PIN_MOD_MODEL_FABLE_EVERY_STAGE_ROLES_OPUS) gets that model for its builders and cap_usd, steward_cap_usd and fix_cap_usd times the price ratio (2 for Fable 5.2, from role_launch.MODEL_PRICES), so the stop lands at the same amount of work. The danger the caps guard: a runaway unattended burn (owner 2026-11-12: "Don't let any burn go to 90M this time ok?"). The evidence the unscaled cap misfires on Fable: 48 of 194 Opus build runs cost over $7.50 and 12 reached $15 (D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\helpers\wm_admit_20261119\build_costs2.txt), so about a quarter of Fable build runs would stop mid-run. The blind judge and the in-game driver are never pinned.
_max_live_doc: At most this many live detached runs on advancing mods at once, the Conductor's own launches included. Raised 2 -> 4 on 2026-11-15 by the owner's card ("Raise to 4"); lowered 4 -> 1 on 2026-11-17 by the owner's word ("Please pause to only one mod at a time to slow the burn" and "Don't stop any current work": live runs finish, nothing new launches while one is live); raised 1 -> 3 on 2026-11-20 by the owner's word ("We should be burning on two mods at the same time", then "This also allows us to work on three mods at once so long as the pipeline can handle that and there's no indication it's breaking again"; the Conductor lowers it again if the pipeline breaks); 3 -> 4 the same evening as the Conductor's act (RIMMANDRAKE_ENACT_CONDUCTOR_MAY_DO_ALL_BUT_FIVE_ACTS): a pipeline repair run counted on GimmeSomeSlack (the second-game split) held one of the three slots, so only two mods ran; back to 3 when no repair run holds a mod slot; set back to 3 on 2026-11-20 5:02 PM PST when that run ended; raised 3 -> 4 on 2026-11-23 4:48 AM PST as the Conductor's act (RIMMANDRAKE_ENACT_CONDUCTOR_MAY_DO_ALL_BUT_FIVE_ACTS) on the owner's words of that night ("keep three mods advancing" and "Let's get Explosive Knockback finished"): four mods advance (FlowWorks, Pyrelands, GimmeSomeSlack 0.2.0, ExplosiveKnockback) and Pyrelands waited on slots with ArchSmall free; the danger this limit guards is machine load (load average 50 on 14 cores made false timing reds at 3:46 AM that night with ten runs live): lower it again if the load average stays over 28; in-game runs stay one at a time per game.
_build_batch_bars_doc: An offline build owing more refused bars than this goes out in even batches of about this many, one builder per batch, each judged on the whole refused set (a batch resolving none of its bars stops the mod as before). Item RIMMANDRAKE_SIZE_DISPATCH_BUILDS_THIRTY_THREE_BARS_ONE_RUN: one builder given all 33 refused Graffiti bars spent USD 7.15 of its 8 and stalled; the steward split them by hand into items of about six. 0 or absent sends the whole set.
_stage_ceiling_doc: Set by the builder of this step: one mod's measured dollars at a stage (every run the status page places there, plus this step's launches, a run with no measured dollars counted at its cap) plus the next run's cap must fit this line, or nothing more launches on that mod at that stage, with a Needs Conductor line: the cap is reserved before launch (RIMMANDRAKE_RESERVE_CAP_BEFORE_LAUNCH). Read at the offline build (a stop), the blind challenge and in-game acceptance (decision ceiling, read each tick). Raised 60 -> 100 on 2026-11-15 by the owner's card ("Raise the limit to $100", item RIMMANDRAKE_RELEASE_STAGE_CEILING_PER_MOD_ONLY_GLOBAL_KNOB).
_settle_s: danger=a run is judged before its published files reach the dispatch clone; ends no work: the run is judged at a later tick
_settle_doc: A run that ended less than this many seconds ago is not judged yet (the tick is 60 s; its published files may not have reached the dispatch clone). Nothing launches on the mod meanwhile.
_game_instances_doc: The games an in-game run may be given on this machine, in order (game_instance.py; item RIMMANDRAKE_LAUNCH_BOTH_GAMES_STEAM_REFUSES_A_BESIDE_B). The owner, 2026-11-16 9:23 PM PST: "don't forget we have two Rimworld games, so I don't want to hear any 'waiting for game'". A game is free when no live in-game run drives it (RM_GAME_INSTANCE in its run record, else a) and its own `rimflow bridge idle` says takeable; the run gets the first free one as RM_GAME_INSTANCE and in its brief. One live driver per game; ["a"] restores the old one-driver rule.
_ingame_doc: In-game acceptance (item RIMMANDRAKE_BUILD_IN_GAME_STAGE_LAUNCHER_PYRELANDS_ARRIVED_FIRST). One live driver (opus, ingame_cap_usd) when visit N is owed (no visit_N folder), nothing is live, just ended or seen as an in-game run on it, a game is free (one live-game driver per game; game_instances), and `rimflow bridge idle` for it says takeable. At most ingame_auto_runs_per_visit automatic runs per visit; a steward run reads each ended visit that has an exit block; one with none, or that it cannot resolve, is a Needs Conductor line; the program never advances. ingame_enabled ships false by the night order of 2026-11-15: the timer starts no live run until the Conductor has run the first visit by hand (maturation.py launch) and sets it true. Set true 2026-11-15 ~05:30 PST by the Conductor (Pyrelands visit 1 ran by hand, ended 05:11; selftests green), ingame_cap_usd 20 -> 30 to match the hand launches ($30 bound; Pyrelands visit 1 spent about $18).
_blind_doc: The blind challenge (item RIMMANDRAKE_BUILD_BLIND_CHALLENGE_LAUNCHER_FOUR_MODS_PARKED). One judge (opus, blind_cap_usd: the hand briefs' $20 bound) when cycle N is owed (no cycle_N folder) and nothing is live, just ended (settle_s) or seen as a blind run since the cycle opened. At most blind_auto_cycles_per_visit automatic cycles per visit, by the owner's condition: "As long as we don't have automated loops rejecting/cycling things, we can't get into too much trouble." A steward run reads each ended cycle below the cycle limit, and one that it cannot resolve is a Needs Conductor line; the program never advances. Raised 1 -> 3 on 2026-11-15 (RIMMANDRAKE_AUTOMATE_MATURATION_HAND_STEPS_MODS_SAT_WAITING) to his own limit, maturation.CYCLE_LIMIT: "after three cycles the Conductor decides; a fourth never starts on its own" (2026-11-13); a cycle ending not met gets one steward run that routes it, never a second.
_stalled_min: danger=a stalled mod goes unseen; ends no work: the stall is alarmed
_steward_doc: maturation_autonomy.py (item RIMMANDRAKE_AUTOMATE_MATURATION_HAND_STEPS_MODS_SAT_WAITING; the owner 2026-11-15: "Get the automation going so things can keep moving even if that means we have to pause them to fix something."). Each Conductor hand step becomes ONE steward run (opus: judging another agent's work, Agent_Policy.md) per state key, capped at steward_cap_usd; each road-back item a steward files gets ONE fixer run (fix_cap_usd). A run that ends with the state unmoved PAUSES the mod (OPS_MATURATION_MOD_PAUSED), never a retry. steward_max_per_version bounds the steward runs on one mod's version; stalled_min is the wait-on-nothing line for OPS_MATURATION_MOD_STALLED.
